canonical_statement: The review aims to bring together key large randomized trials that established pharmacological therapies recommended or considered to improve outcomes in heart failure.

Trial selection included studies that substantially influenced international guideline recommendations or clinical practice, and the evidence was organized by drug class and heart-failure ejection-fraction phenotype.

The review describes loop diuretics as a cornerstone for relief of congestion and symptoms but not as classic mortality-reducing disease-modifying therapy because well-powered outcome trials are lacking.
Differences in trial populations, design, background therapy, and ejection-fraction thresholds limit direct comparisons across the heart-failure trials summarized in the review.
The review concludes that multiple drug classes reduce mortality and heart-failure hospitalization in HFrEF and form the basis of contemporary quadruple therapy.
The review concludes that evidence in HFmrEF and HFpEF is more heterogeneous and identifies SGLT2 inhibitors as the only class with consistent benefit across the full LVEF spectrum.
The authors identify a persistent gap between guideline recommendations and real-world heart-failure treatment implementation.
The authors identify better representation of under-represented trial populations and development of precision-medicine approaches as future research priorities in heart failure.
The review reports that CONSENSUS (1987) compared Enalapril with Placebo for All-cause mortality at 6 months: relative risk reduction percent 40; P=0.002; 26% vs 44%.
The review reports that SOLVD-Treatment (1991) compared Enalapril with Placebo for All-cause mortality: risk ratio 0.84 (95% CI 0.74-0.95); P=0.004; 35% vs 40%.
The review reports that SAVE (1992) compared Captopril with Placebo for All-cause mortality: risk ratio 0.81 (95% CI 0.68-0.97); P=0.019; 20% vs 25%.
The review reports that AIRE (1993) compared Ramipril with Placebo for All-cause mortality: risk ratio 0.73 (95% CI 0.6-0.88); P=0.002; 17% vs 23%.
The review reports that TRACE (1995) compared Trandolapril with Placebo for All-cause mortality: risk ratio 0.78 (95% CI 0.67-0.91); P=0.001; 35% vs 42%.
The review reports that ATLAS (1999) compared High-dose lisinopril with Low-dose lisinopril for All-cause mortality: hazard ratio 0.92 (95% CI 0.82-1.03); P=0.128; 20% vs 21%.

population.label: Chronic symptomatic HF, NYHA II-IV, LVEF <=30%

canonical_statement: The review states that SGLT2 inhibitors became the first pharmacological class with class I recommendations across heart failure irrespective of ejection fraction, including HFmrEF and HFpEF.
The review states that the strongest current evidence for incretin-based therapy in heart failure pertains to patients with obesity and HFpEF.

The review reports funding from Wroclaw Medical University grants SUBZ.A460.25.57 and IDUB.A46B.24.002 and from the university development strategy "UMW in the Light of Scientific Excellence 2024-2026".

The review discloses that multiple authors received consulting fees, honoraria, research support, travel support, or advisory-board roles from pharmaceutical and medical-device companies; the declarations list the specific relationships by author.
The authors state that the article generated and analyzed no original data and therefore has no data available for sharing.
